newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong protesters condemn interim legislature.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong protesters condemn interim legislature.

text.p: Hong Kong democracy campaigners staged protests on Friday against Beijing's plan to scrap the colony's elected legislature, the day before a China-appointed committee is to select the members of a replacement council.
"Oppose the provisional legislature, oppose the rubber stamp," chanted members of Hong Kong's Democratic Party outside the local branch of Xinhua News Agency, China's de facto embassy here.

China has sworn to scrap the present, elected Legislative Council when it takes over Hong Kong at midnight June 30 next year because it did not approve democratic reforms enacted by the colonial administration.
An interim provisional chamber is to be chosen by a Beijing-controlled 400-member Selection Committee on Saturday in Shenzhen, located in China just across the border from Hong Kong.

"It is totally unacceptable," independent legislator Emily Lau said at a separate protest. "There is no legal and constitutional basis for that body, and also the Chinese government is using that body to kick out people who they do not like.
"We think that with the end of colonial rule the only way to set up a legitimate legislature is to allow the Hong Kong people to elect it through universal sufferage," she said.

Another group of 10 demonstrators tried to protest at a bus station where members of the Selection Committee boarded a coach for Shenzhen, but were kept at a distance from the vehicle by police who clashed with protesters.

"The Selection Committee betrays Hong Kong people," they shouted. Protesters said the interim legislature violated the territory's post-handover constitution and a 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration governing the sovereignty transfer.
